title: Concentration, extraction and quantification of SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater via droplet digital PCR
author: Jim Huang

Filtration to remove particulates Stericup Quick Release-GP Sterile Vacuum Filtration System Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #S2GPU02RE Clarification of the sample is necessary to avoid clogging at the ultrafiltration step. This protocol uses filtration but centrifugation can also be employed and is cheaper. Pass each sample through a 0.22μM PES filter (diameter >8 cm)

Innovaprep Ultrafiltration Ultrafiltration PS Hollow Fiber Concentrating Pipette Tips - Unirradiated - 200pk Innovaprep Catalog #CC08004-200 FluidPrep Elution Fluid Can - Tris Innovaprep Catalog #HC08001 Insert a fresh ultrafiltration tip into the device Insert the tip into the sample Start Run (see note for program details) If run stops before all liquid is aspirated, Press Return and Start Run again. This is more likely to happen with turbid samples, or if the tip is faulty. Remove the empty sample bottle and replace with a 15 ml conical tube Press Elute Store the eluate on ice until all samples have been concentrated Transfer 140 μl of eluate to a fresh tube containing 560 μl of Qiagen AVL buffer and mix well before proceeding to Step 8 The remaining eluate can be stored at -80°C The eluate volume is usually in the range of 200-800 μl (50-100 fold concentration) The volume should be estimated by drawing the eluate up into a 1ml pipette tip and recorded as it is needed to calculate the final viral load. Innovaprep Program Details These settings should allow efficient aspiration and elution without interruption using the ultrafiltration tips on wastewwater that has been passed through a 0.22uM pre-filter. Enter eluate volume for Sample 1 Enter eluate volume for Sample 2

Spike Lysis Quick Extract DNA Extraction Solution Lucigen Catalog #QE0905T Add 5μl Quick Extract DNA Extraction Solution to 10μl BCoV Spike from Step 5 Heat in thermocycler at 65°C for 15 min then 98°C for 2 min, then 4°C forever Add 85 μl H 2 O and store on ice for use in ddPCR Can store at -80°C for reference Altenative Lysis Protocol using GT Molecular Lysis Buffer

QiaAMP Viral RNA Extraction Protocol Wear gloves, labcoat and goggles or glasses. Virus is inactivated upon 10 minute incubation with AVL and can be removed from the Biosafety Cabinet at that point. NEVER mix Qiagen reagents that contain guanidinium with bleach as it results in toxic fumes! After 10 min incubation, briefly spin down the AVL/Eluate mix Add 560 μl 100% ethanol Vortex for 15 sec Apply 630 μl to Epoch column in a 2ml collection tube Centrifuge 6,000xg for 1 minute. Decant the filtrate Load the remaining sample onto the column Centrifuge 6,000xg for 1 minute Add 500μl of AW1 and spin 1 minute at 6,000xg for 1 minute Add 500μl of AW2 and spin at max speed for 3 minutes Place the column in a fresh 2mL collection tube and spin again for 1 minute at max speed Place the column in a fresh, labeled 1.5ml tube and add 60μl of RNase free water to each column Incubate for 1 minute Spin at 6,000xg for 3 minutes Store samples on ice (if using immediately) or at -80°C for long term storage By this stage there is generally very little RNA, so quality control via nanodrop is not informative. If samples are frozen before processing then more RNA is recovered, presumably because freezing lyses cells and microbes and releases nucleic acids. Double volume of eluate can be loaded onto a single Epoch column to increase sensitivity. In this case, double volumes of ethanol and AVL must also be used.

SARS-CoV-2 Positive Control This reagent is used as a positive control for ddPCR detection of SARS-CoV-2. The variant listed below works well with the primer set described here, other variants may or may not be detected. SARS-Related Coronavirus 2 Isolate USA-WA1/2020 Heat Inactivated BEI Resources Catalog #NR-52286 QuickExtract DNA Extraction Solution Lucigen Catalog #QE09050 Add 5μl Quick Extract DNA Extraction Solution to 10μl heat-inactivated virus Heat in thermocycler at 65°C for 15 min then 98°C for 2 min, then 4°C forever Add 85 μl H 2 O Dilute to desired concentration, aliquot and store at -80°C The resulting solution will be at around 10 5 copies per μl. We recommend further dilution to between 10 and 100 copies per μl for use as a positive control in RT-ddPCR.

Primer / Probe Mixes See Materials for Sequences. Primer/probe mixes are made as described below, aliquoted, and stored at -20°C in the dark. After thawing on ice, aliquots are stored at 4°C. 100 μM Forward Primer 100 μl 100 μM Reverse Primer 100 μl 100 μM Probe 25 μl H 2 O 1275 μl

Reaction Set Up Thaw all required reagents on ice: > Reverse Transcriptase > 300mM DTT > Primer Probe Mixes > BioRad 1-step RT-ddPCR supermix for probes > Wastewater RNA > Positive controls SARS-CoV-2 /BCoV Reactions Create a mastermix sufficient for all reactions adding reagents in the order shown Include 1-2 safety reactions to ensure there is enough mastermix i.e. if you have 10 reactions make a mastermix for 11-12 reactions Pipette each template RNA into one well of an 8-tube strip. Add 13µl mastermix to each well Vortex briefly and spin to the bottom of the tube F+ / PMMoV Reactions Dilute template RNA 1:100 for F+ and PMMoV reactions - add 3 μl RNA to 273 μl H 2 O Create a mastermix sufficient for all reactions adding reagents in the order shown Include 1-2 safety reactions to ensure there is enough mastermix i.e. if you have 10 reactions make a mastermix for 11-12 reactions Pipette each diluted template RNA into one well of an 8-tube strip. Add 13µl mastermix to each well Add ddPCR buffer control for probes to any empty wells in the 8 tube strip Mix and spin to the bottom of the tube It is important to include both positive and negative controls. The negative control should contain H 2 O instead of RNA template.
Thermocycling Using a BioRad C1000 Touch deep-well device: 50°C for 1 hr (reverse transcription step) 95°C for 10 min [94°C for 30 sec; 55°C for 1 min] x 44; 98°C for 10 min 4°C forever

steps.title: Prepare Biosafety Cabinet
steps.instruction: Wipe down the biosafety cabinet (BSC) with 70 % ethanol. Ensure the BSC airflow is not blocked, especially when processing ≥10 samples.

steps.title: Prepare BCoV Spike Reagents
steps.instruction: Reconstitute Bovilis Coronavirus Intranasal Vaccine (Merck, Catalog #43817, 10‑dose lyophilized) in 5 ml PBS containing 0.01 % Tween 20; aliquot and store at –80 °C. Prepare a 1:500 working stock in PBS + 0.01 % Tween 20, aliquot 500 µl, store at –80 °C; the working stock should contain ≈3000 genome copies µl⁻¹.

steps.title: Thaw BCoV Aliquots
steps.instruction: Thaw on ice a volume of BCoV working stock sufficient for all samples using the formula (N + 2) × 14.5 µl, where N is the number of wastewater samples; keep the thawed aliquot on ice until use.

steps.title: Pre‑Treat Wastewater Samples
steps.instruction: Perform all steps on ice. For each 40 ml wastewater sample (adjusted to exactly 40 ml if necessary) add 400 µl of 10 % Tween 20 and 14.3 µl of the thawed BCoV spike (≈30‑50 000 genome copies). Vortex, then centrifuge at 16 000 g for 5 min. Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube, mix well by inverting, and keep the remaining BCoV spike on ice for later steps.

steps.title: Run Innovaprep Ultrafiltration
steps.instruction: Perform the Start‑Up Procedure on the Innovaprep instrument, insert the effluent tube into a beaker containing 10 % bleach, load the pre‑treated sample (up to 80 ml per tip) and run according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Collect the eluate (total volume I_P, typically 200‑900 µl). Ensure sufficient elution fluid, ultrafiltration tips, and other consumables are available.

steps.title: Generate Droplets for ddPCR
steps.instruction: Place a DG8 cartridge in its holder and close it. Using a multi‑channel pipette, transfer 20 µl of each ddPCR reaction mix to the “Sample” wells and dispense 70 µl AutoDG oil to the “Oil” wells. Seal the cartridge with a clean gasket, insert it into the droplet generator and press Start. Gently transfer the generated droplets with a P200 pipette into a 96‑well plate. Repeat for all samples. Turn on the plate sealer, place a foil seal on the plate and seal at 180 °C for 5 seconds (AutoDG oil is preferred for higher droplet counts).

steps.title: Read Droplets on QX200
steps.instruction: Allow 2.5 min per sample plus 10‑15 min for set‑up. Open the QX200 droplet reader, insert the sealed 96‑well plate, lock the metal grid and close the device. Launch the QuantaSoft software, select Absolute Quantification (ABS), assign Channel 1 FAM to SARS‑CoV‑2 (or F⁺) and Channel 2 HEX to BCoV (or PMMoV), and load the 1‑step RT‑ddPCR kit probes. Click RUN to acquire data.

steps.title: Set Analysis Thresholds
steps.instruction: In QuantaSoft, go to the Droplets tab, select all wells and verify that each well contains >10 000 droplets (typical range 12 000‑19 000). In the 2‑D Amplitude view, select wells containing the SARS‑CoV‑2/BCoV probes and position the pink (+) thresholds between positive and negative droplet clouds. Switch to the 1‑D view and ensure thresholds lie above all droplets in the no‑template control. Set separate thresholds for the F⁺/PMMoV wells (do not set them simultaneously).

steps.title: Export Quantasoft Data
steps.instruction: In either the 1‑D or 2‑D Amplitude view, select all wells, open the Well Data panel menu and choose “Export to Excel”. Export at minimum the following columns: Well, Sample, Target, Copies/20 µl, Accepted [# droplets], PoissonConfMax, PoissonConfMin.

steps.title: Calculate SARS‑CoV‑2 Copies per L
steps.instruction:
Use the exported copies per 20 µl (C) and the following parameters: Wastewater volume W = 40 ml; total Innovaprep eluate volume I_P (200‑900 µl); eluate volume used for RNA extraction I_E = 140 µl; total RNA eluate volume R_T = 60 µl; RNA volume added to ddPCR R_U = 8.2 µl. Compute genomes per litre with:
Genomes/L = C × (R_T/R_U) × (1000/W) × (I_P/I_E).
For this protocol the constant simplifies to 1.3066 × C × I_P. The limit of detection (LOD) is ≈3‑5 copies per reaction (≈3 000‑5 000 copies L⁻¹) and the limit of quantification (LOQ) is ≈15 copies per reaction (≈13 000‑15 000 copies L⁻¹).

steps.title: Calculate Endogenous Control Copies per L
steps.instruction:
Apply the same formula as above but multiply by 100 to account for the 100‑fold dilution of the PMMoV and F⁺ templates:
Genomes/L = C × (R_T/R_U) × (1000/W) × (I_P/I_E) × 100.
With the protocol constants this becomes 130.66 × C × I_P. Expected ranges: PMMoV ≈10⁸‑10⁹ copies L⁻¹; F⁺ coliphage ≈10⁷‑10⁸ copies L⁻¹.

steps.title: Determine BCoV Recovery Efficiency
steps.instruction:
First calculate the number of BCoV copies added at the start:
BCoV copies_in = BCoV copies_20µl × 14.3 µl × 10 ÷ 8.2 µl = BCoV copies_20µl × 17.439.
Then compute the percentage recovered from the whole 40 ml sample:
BCoV recovery (%) = 100 × BCoV copies_20µl × (R_T/R_U) ÷ BCoV copies_in × (I_E/I_P).
Acceptable recovery is 15‑25 %; values <5 % suggest RNA degradation, spike loss, or RT inhibition.

description: Quality Controls and Troubleshooting One possible use of the controls is for normalization. In our experience with Colorado WWTPs normalization to either exogenous (BCoV) or endogenous controls (PMMoV, F+) did not improve correlations with community infection rate or reduce variability. The controls can also be used to detect failure of reactions due to inhibitors and to distinguish between inhibition and degradation: Both the reverse transcription step and the PCR step can be inhibited by compounds that carry through the extraction step (either reagents such as phenol or guanidine, or contaminants such as humic acids). Inhibition of the RT step will generally result in fewer positive droplets (because there will be less cDNA produced) and confounds accurate quantification. Inhibition of the PCR step can result in reduced fluorescence amplitude i.e. poor separation of the positive and negative droplets, because each cycle will produce fewer copies of the cDNA template). This may not affect quantification if the separation remains adequate for threshold setting. Inhibition is not template specific - all targets in a reaction mix will be affected. Low BCoV recovery (<5%) can indicate inhibition of the RT step. Importantly, inhibition can often be abrogated by using less of the RNA containing the inhibitor. Therefore the PMMoV/F+ reaction will generally give good results even when inhibitors are present because it uses a 100 fold diluted RNA template. If BCoV recovery fails QC, it is helpful to rerun the reaction with half or quarter the amount of RNA template (assuming the SARS-N1 levels are high enough to still be detected). In contrast, degradation of the RNA sample will result in fewer positive droplets for all four targets (i.e. Low BCOV recovery and low PMMoV/F+). This problem can only be remedied by repeating the extraction to make fresh RNA.
